title: Tokenizer ↔ Model Mismatch (Vocabulary / Special Tokens / Shape Errors)
description: Troubleshooting and resolving tokenizer-model mismatch failures, including vocabulary size mismatches, special token misalignments, and embedding dimension conflicts.
name: Tokenizer ↔ Model Mismatch (Vocabulary / Special Tokens / Shape Errors)

quick_identification.description: Compare vocabulary sizes; mismatch indicates incompatible tokenizer-model pair.

quick_identification.check: Token IDs exceed model embedding dimensions
Special token IDs differ between tokenizer and model config
quick_identification.description: Compare tokenizer.pad_token_id, bos_token_id, eos_token_id with model.config equivalents.

symptoms.description: Forward pass crashes with index out of bounds in the embedding layer or a CUDA assert triggered by an invalid token ID.
symptoms.error_message: IndexError: index out of range in self or CUDA error: device-side assert triggered.

symptoms.description: Loading state dict fails because saved embedding weights have a different shape than the model's embedding layer.
symptoms.error_message: RuntimeError: Error(s) in loading state_dict: size mismatch for model.embed_tokens.weight.

symptoms.description: Model generates coherent-looking but semantically wrong tokens; vocabulary mapping is shifted or corrupted.
symptoms.error_message: No explicit error; outputs are nonsensical.

symptoms.description: Model does not recognize <pad>, <s>, </s>, or other special tokens; they are treated as ordinary subwords.
symptoms.error_message: No explicit error; attention mask or generation length is wrong.
symptoms.where_appears: Padding, generation stopping, chat template formatting.

root_causes.explanation: The tokenizer vocabulary was extended but the model embedding matrix was not resized, so token IDs map to non-existent embedding rows.
recognition_clues: Error occurs immediately on the first forward pass with tokenized input.
Mismatch appears after tokenizer.add_tokens() or tokenizer.add_special_tokens().
root_causes.typical_environment: Fine-tuning with domain-specific vocabulary, multilingual model adaptation, code model training.

root_causes.explanation: AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained() loads tokenizer from checkpoint A while AutoModel.from_pretrained() loads weights from checkpoint B, so vocabulary mappings differ.
recognition_clues: Tokenizer and model are loaded from different paths or repo IDs.
Generation quality degrades after checkpoint swap.
root_causes.typical_environment: Experiment tracking with mixed artifacts, manual checkpoint management, adapter or LoRA loading with base model mismatch.

root_causes.explanation: Tokenizer assigns different IDs to <pad>, <s>, </s>, or <unk> than the model expects, so the model reads the wrong embeddings for those positions.
recognition_clues: Generation does not stop at eos_token_id.
Padding is ignored because pad_token_id maps to a meaningful token in the model vocabulary.
root_causes.typical_environment: Chat model fine-tuning, custom chat templates, legacy model conversion.

root_causes.cause: Embedding Matrix Not Resized After Tokenizer Extension
root_causes.explanation: Adding tokens increases vocabulary size, but model.resize_token_embeddings() was not called, leaving the embedding matrix with the old dimensions.
recognition_clues: tokenizer.vocab_size increased after add_tokens() but model.config.vocab_size did not.
Error appears only after tokenizer modification.
root_causes.typical_environment: Continual pretraining, domain adaptation, instruction tuning with new special tokens.

root_causes.cause: Legacy Tokenizer File with Updated Model
root_causes.explanation: An old tokenizer.json or vocab.txt is used with newer model weights, so vocabulary ordering or special-token handling diverges.
recognition_clues: The model repo contains multiple tokenizer files.
Loading occurs from local paths instead of the Hub.
The model was converted between formats.
root_causes.typical_environment: Model format conversions, offline deployments with partial file copies, custom model merges.

root_causes.explanation: The underlying SentencePiece model file has different vocabulary than the tokenizer JSON config, so token conversion becomes non-idempotent.
recognition_clues: Decoding differs from re-encoding the same text.
root_causes.typical_environment: Custom SentencePiece training, vocabulary pruning, tokenizer merging from different sources.

investigation_checklist.description: Compare tokenizer.pad_token_id, bos_token_id, eos_token_id with model.config.

investigation_checklist.check: Check tokenizer and model source paths
investigation_checklist.description: Verify both were loaded from the same checkpoint or compatible versions.

investigation_checklist.check: Check for tokenizer modifications without embedding resize
investigation_checklist.description: Search code for add_tokens or add_special_tokens without resize_token_embeddings().
For SPM tokenizers, verify sp_model vocabulary matches JSON config.
Verify tokenizer.decode(tokenizer.encode(text)) == text for sample inputs.

diagnostic_commands.command: python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel; t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('model_name'); m = AutoModel.from_pretrained('model_name'); print(f'Tokenizer: {len(t)}, Model: {m.config.vocab_size}')"
diagnostic_commands.interpretation: Mismatch indicates an incompatible tokenizer-model pair.

diagnostic_commands.expected_output: Embedding rows: N where N >= max token ID.
diagnostic_commands.interpretation: If N < tokenizer vocab size, resize is needed.

diagnostic_commands.command: python -c "print(f'Tokenizer pad: {tokenizer.pad_token_id}, Model pad: {model.config.pad_token_id}'); print(f'Tokenizer eos: {tokenizer.eos_token_id}, Model eos: {model.config.eos_token_id}')"
diagnostic_commands.expected_output: Matching IDs for all special tokens.
diagnostic_commands.interpretation: Mismatch causes padding and generation boundary failures.

diagnostic_commands.command: python -c "text = 'Hello world'; ids = tokenizer.encode(text); decoded = tokenizer.decode(ids); print(f'Round-trip: {text == decoded}'); print(f'Max ID: {max(ids)}, Vocab: {tokenizer.vocab_size}')"
diagnostic_commands.expected_output: Round-trip: True, max ID less than vocab size.
diagnostic_commands.interpretation: False or out-of-bounds IDs indicate vocabulary corruption.

diagnostic_tests.test: Encode a sample corpus and check all IDs are within model embedding bounds.
diagnostic_tests.command: python -c "ids = tokenizer.encode(corpus, add_special_tokens=False); max_id = max(ids); embed_size = model.get_input_embeddings().weight.shape[0]; print(f'Max ID: {max_id}, Embed size: {embed_size}, OK: {max_id < embed_size}')"
diagnostic_tests.next_action: Resize embeddings or reload a matching tokenizer.

diagnostic_tests.test: Verify special tokens map to the same IDs in tokenizer and model.
diagnostic_tests.command:
python -c "for tok in ['', '', '', '']: tid = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(tok); mid = getattr(model.config, f'{tok.strip(\"

\")}_token_id', None); print(f'{tok}: tokenizer={tid}, model={mid}, match={tid==mid}')"
diagnostic_tests.next_action: Synchronize special token IDs or update model config.

diagnostic_tests.test: Check whether newly added tokens have valid embeddings.
diagnostic_tests.command: python -c "emb = model.get_input_embeddings().weight; new_start = model.config.vocab_size - num_added; new_embs = emb[new_start:]; print(f'New embed mean: {new_embs.mean():.4f}, std: {new_embs.std():.4f}')"
diagnostic_tests.expected_result: Non-zero mean and standard deviation indicating initialized embeddings.
diagnostic_tests.interpretation: Zero or NaN values indicate failed initialization.
diagnostic_tests.next_action: Reinitialize new embeddings or re-run resize with proper init.

solutions.solution: Resize Token Embeddings After Vocabulary Extension
solutions.permanent_fix: Wrap tokenizer extension in a utility that automatically resizes embeddings and initializes new tokens.
steps: Identify added tokens: num_added = tokenizer.add_tokens(new_tokens).
Resize embeddings: model.resize_token_embeddings(len(tokenizer)).
Initialize new embeddings: model.get_input_embeddings().weight.data[-num_added:].normal_(mean=0.0, std=0.02).
Tie weights if applicable: model.tie_weights().
Verify: assert model.get_input_embeddings().weight.shape[0] == len(tokenizer).
tradeoffs: Increases model parameter count, with minor memory overhead.
New tokens start untrained and need sufficient training steps.
solutions.performance_impact: Negligible; only increases embedding matrix size.
works_for: Special token additions for instruction tuning.

solutions.quick_fix: Load both tokenizer and model from the identical checkpoint path.
solutions.permanent_fix: Use model cards and revision pinning to ensure tokenizer-model consistency.
steps: Identify model checkpoint: model_name_or_path.
Load tokenizer from the same path: AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name_or_path).
Verify alignment: assert tokenizer.vocab_size == model.config.vocab_size.
For adapters or LoRA, ensure base model and tokenizer come from the same base checkpoint.
Pin revision with from_pretrained(..., revision="abc123") for reproducibility.
tradeoffs: May require re-downloading large tokenizer files.
Adapter training may need restart if the base model was wrong.
solutions.performance_impact: None; corrects mapping without architectural change.
solutions.verification: tokenizer.name_or_path == model.name_or_path and vocab sizes match.

solutions.quick_fix: Manually align special token IDs between tokenizer and model config.
solutions.permanent_fix: Use tokenizer.save_pretrained() and model.config.save_pretrained() to persist synchronized state.
steps: Inspect current IDs: tokenizer.pad_token_id, model.config.pad_token_id.
Set tokenizer to match model: tokenizer.pad_token_id = model.config.pad_token_id.
Or set model to match tokenizer: model.config.pad_token_id = tokenizer.pad_token_id.
Repeat for bos_token_id, eos_token_id, and unk_token_id.
Update generation config: model.generation_config.pad_token_id = tokenizer.pad_token_id.
Save synchronized configs.
tradeoffs: Changing model config may affect downstream uses.
Some models have hardcoded special-token assumptions in the forward pass.
works_for: Custom fine-tuning with changed special tokens.
solutions.verification: All special token IDs match and generation stops correctly at eos_token_id.

solutions.quick_fix: Delete local tokenizer cache and re-download from the Hugging Face Hub.
solutions.permanent_fix: Use snapshot_download with explicit file filtering to ensure complete tokenizer files.
steps: Clear cache: rm -rf ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--model-name.
Re-download: AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("org/model", force_download=True).
Verify file completeness: check for tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json, and special_tokens_map.json.
For SentencePiece, verify the .model` file exists and matches the JSON config.
Compare SHA with model card metadata if available.
tradeoffs: Requires internet access and re-download time.
Cache clearing affects all models from the same namespace.
solutions.verification: Round-trip encoding works and file hashes match the Hub.

solutions.quick_fix: Use the tokenizers library to merge vocabularies with explicit ID mapping.
solutions.permanent_fix: Train a new unified SentencePiece model on a combined corpus.
steps: Extract vocabularies: vocab_a = tokenizer_a.get_vocab(), vocab_b = tokenizer_b.get_vocab().
Create a merged vocabulary with stable ID assignment.
Map old IDs to new IDs for both tokenizers.
Re-embed model weights using an ID mapping matrix.
Save the new tokenizer and remapped model weights.
tradeoffs: Complex implementation; requires custom mapping logic.
works_for: Multi-model ensembles with a shared tokenizer.
Domain adaptation with incompatible base tokenizers.
solutions.verification: Both original tokenizers produce valid IDs in the merged vocabulary.

practices: Always load tokenizer and model from the identical checkpoint path.
Wrap add_tokens() calls with automatic resize_token_embeddings() in training scripts.
Pin model revisions in production configs to prevent silent tokenizer updates.
Run a vocabulary alignment check as the first step in training startup.
Validate tokenizer.vocab_size == model.config.vocab_size in CI/CD before deployment.
Version tokenizer files alongside model weights in the same artifact.
Use the transformers pipeline abstraction only when it preserves tokenizer-model pairing.
Log tokenizer and model checkpoint hashes at training start for audit.
Alert when len(tokenizer) != model.config.vocab_size in training jobs.
Track generation perplexity; sudden spikes can indicate vocabulary misalignment.
Monitor for device-side assert triggered errors as an early indicator.
Compare training loss curves against baselines; flat loss with high norm can suggest embedding issues.
Never call tokenizer.add_tokens() without immediate model.resize_token_embeddings().
Always assert special token ID equality before starting the training loop.
Use tokenizer.encode(..., add_special_tokens=True) consistently with model expectations.
Save both tokenizer and model config after any special-token modification.

common_misconceptions.reality: add_tokens() increases len(tokenizer) but not vocab_size; use len(tokenizer) for embedding resize.

common_misconceptions.misconception: AutoTokenizer and AutoModel from the same repo name guarantee compatibility
common_misconceptions.reality: Different revisions, local caches, or adapter loading can silently mismatch; always verify vocab sizes.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Special tokens are just strings, so their IDs do not matter if the string is in vocabulary
common_misconceptions.reality: Model forward pass and generation logic depend on specific ID values for padding, masking, and stopping criteria.

false_positive_cases.case: CUDA device-side assert from unrelated index error
false_positive_cases.why_it_looks_similar: Same error message as tokenizer mismatch.
false_positive_cases.how_to_distinguish: Check whether the error occurs in non-embedding layers and validate data-loader indices.

false_positive_cases.why_it_looks_similar: tokenizer.vocab_size < original, and model may have larger embeddings.
false_positive_cases.how_to_distinguish: Pruning is deliberate; embeddings were resized down or unused rows are masked.

false_positive_cases.why_it_looks_similar: Embedding shape differs from vocabulary size.
false_positive_cases.how_to_distinguish: The model config specifies tie_word_embeddings=False and uses adaptive or factorized embeddings.

tradeoffs: Requires a large corpus for training.

escalation_paths.when_to_use: Frequent out-of-vocabulary issues with the current tokenizer.
tradeoffs: May degrade performance on some languages.
